name: Custom Background
summary: Build a custom background by choosing one feature from another background, any two skill proficiencies, and a total of two tool proficiencies or languages. Use a background equipment package or spend coin on gear.

name: Acolyte
summary: As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I look up to a hero of my faith and keep pointing to their deeds as an example.
I can find common ground even with my worst enemies and always push for peace.
I see omens everywhere; the gods are always trying to tell us something.
No hardship can shake my cheerful, hopeful outlook.
I quote scripture and sayings for every occasion, not always correctly.
I swing between accepting other faiths and condemning them.
I enjoy fine food, comfort and high society; roughing it is not for me.
Years in the temple left me with little idea how to deal with ordinary people.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Tradition. The old rites of worship and sacrifice must be kept alive. (Lawful)
Charity. I always help those in need, whatever it costs me. (Good)
Change. I must help bring about the changes the gods are working in the world. (Chaotic)
Power. One day I want to reach the top of my faith's hierarchy. (Lawful)
Faith. My god will guide me; if I work hard, things will turn out well. (Lawful)
Aspiration. I try to live up to my god's teachings and earn their favor. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: I would die to recover a long-lost relic of my faith.
Someday I'll get even with the corrupt temple leaders who branded me a heretic.
I owe my life to the priest who took me in when my parents died.
Everything I do is for the common people.
I'll do anything to protect the temple I served in.
I protect a sacred text that my enemies want to destroy as heresy.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I judge others harshly, and myself even more so.
I trust the people in power in my temple far too much.
Anyone who claims to share my faith gets my blind trust.
My thinking is rigid, even when I need to bend.
I distrust strangers and expect the worst of them.
Once I pick a goal, I let everything else in my life slide.

name: Anthropologist
summary: Before becoming an adventurer, you spent much of your adult life away from your homeland, living among people different from your kin. You came to understand these foreign cultures and the ways of their people, who eventually treated you as one of their own. One culture had more of an influence on you than any other, shaping your beliefs and customs. Choose a race whose culture you've adopted.

name: Archaeologist
summary: Prior to becoming an adventurer, you spent most of your young life crawling around in the dust, pilfering relics of questionable value from crypts and ruins. Though you managed to sell a few of your discoveries and earn enough coin to buy proper adventuring gear, you have held onto an item that has great emotional value to you. Roll on the Signature Item table to see what you have, or choose an item from the table.

choices.label: Choose cartographer's tools or navigator's tools

name: Ashari
summary: You were raised among the Ashari of Tal'Dorei, guardians of the elemental rifts. Living beside wild elemental magic has attuned you to it.
skillProficiencies: Nature, plus your choice of Arcana or Survival

name: Astral Drifter
summary: You are 20d6 years older than you look, because you have spent that much time in the Astral Sea without aging.
source: Spelljamer: Adventures in Space - Astral Adventurer's Guide

name: Athlete
summary: You strive to perfect yourself physically and in execution of everything you do. The thrill of competition lights fire in your blood, and the roar of the crowd drives you forward. Tales of your exploits precede you and might open doors or loosen tongues.

name: Azorius Functionary
summary: You have the authority to enforce the laws of Ravnica, and that status inspires a certain amount of respect and even fear in the populace. People mind their manners in your presence and avoid drawing your attention: they assume you have the right to be wherever you are. Showing your Azorius insignia gets you an audience with anyone you want to talk to (though it might cause more problems than it solves when you're dealing with incorrigible lawbreakers). If you abuse this privilege, though, you can get in serious trouble with your superiors and even be stripped of your position.

name: Black Fist Double Agent
summary: You are an informant for the Tears of Virulence who now lord over Phlan, but are also a double agent for the original town guard of Phlan, the Black Fist. For the Tears you’ve been tasked with ferreting out the secrets of Phlan's criminal underworld, insurgency, and the common peoples of Phlan. In exchange for reporting on the activities of dissenters, criminals, and other rebel elements, the Tears of Virulence leave you alone to conduct your affairs in peace.

choices.label: Choose one artisan's tool or gaming set

name: Boros Legionnaire
summary: You have an established place in the hierarchy of the Boros Legion. You can requisition simple equipment for temporary use, and you can gain access to any Boros garrison in Ravnica, where you can rest in safety and receive the attention of medics. You are also paid a salary of 1 gp (a Boros-minted 1 zino coin) per week, which (combined with free lodging in your garrison) enables you to maintain a poor lifestyle between adventures.

name: Caravan Specialist
summary: You are used to life on the road. You pride yourself at having traveled every major tradeway in the Moonsea region, including the best back roads and shortcuts. When traveling these roads, you know where the best inns, campsites, and water sources are located, as well as potential locations of danger such as ambush. Having worked the roads as long as you have, you have made many acquaintances and find it easy to pick up information and rumors floating from town to town. You are skilled with beasts of burden and handling and repairing wagons of all kinds.

name: Celebrity Adventurer's Scion
summary: Your family name strikes fear and admiration in the hearts of the common folk - but that's got nothing to do with you. Songs and stories celebrating the adventuring exploits of your famous parent are widely known. Kids across the land grew up wishing they were you. But being the child of a famous adventurer wasn't all hugs and kisses.

name: Charlatan
summary: You have always had a way with people: you know what makes them tick and how to sell them a lie. You keep a second, forged identity ready for when you need it.

tables.title: Favorite Scheme
entries: I rig games of chance.
I shave coins or forge documents.
I worm my way into people's lives, find their weak spots and take their money.
I put on new identities like other people change clothes.
I run sleight-of-hand cons on street corners.
I sell worthless junk as if it were treasure.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I fall in and out of love easily and am always chasing someone new.
I have a joke for every moment, especially the wrong ones.
Flattery is how I get what I want.
I can't say no to a big risky bet with a big payoff.
I lie about almost everything, even when there's no reason to.
Sarcasm and insults are my favorite weapons.
I carry several holy symbols and call on whichever god fits the moment.
Anything valuable I see tends to end up in my pocket.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Independence. I'm a free spirit; no one tells me what to do. (Chaotic)
Fairness. I never con people who can't afford to lose a few coins. (Lawful)
Charity. I give my ill-gotten gains to those who really need them. (Good)
Creativity. I never pull the same con twice. (Chaotic)
Friendship. Things come and go; friends are forever. (Good)
Aspiration. I'm going to make something of myself. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: I conned the wrong person and must keep them away from me and my own.
My mentor taught me everything; they're a terrible person and probably in jail now.
I have a child who doesn't know me, and I'm trying to make the world better for them.
My noble family's land and title were stolen, and I'll take them back.
A powerful person killed someone I loved, and I'll have my revenge.
I ruined someone who didn't deserve it, and I'm trying to make amends.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I can't resist a pretty face.
I'm always in debt; my dishonest money goes on luxuries faster than it comes in.
I'm sure no one could ever con me the way I con others.
I'm too greedy to pass up a gamble with money on the line.
I can't stop myself from swindling people more powerful than me.
When things go bad I save my own skin, and I hate myself for it.

name: City Watch
summary: Rarer than watch or patrol members are a community's investigators, who are responsible for solving crimes after the fact. Though such folk are seldom found in rural areas, nearly every settlement of decent size has at least one or two watch members who have the skill to investigate crime scenes and track down criminals. If your prior experience is as an investigator, you have proficiency in Investigation rather than Athletics.

name: Clan Crafter
summary: As well respected as clan crafters are among outsiders, no one esteems them quite so highly as dwarves do. You always have free room and board in any place where shield dwarves or gold dwarves dwell, and the individuals in such a settlement might vie among themselves to determine who can offer you (and possibly your compatriots) the finest accommodations and assistance.

name: Cloistered Scholar
summary: Though others must often endure extensive interviews and significant fees to gain access to even the most common archives in your library, you have free and easy access to the majority of the library, though it might also have repositories of lore that are too valuable, magical, or secret to permit anyone immediate access.
skillProficiencies: History, plus your choice of one from among Arcana, Nature, and Religion

name: Cormanthor Refugee
summary: You are one of hundreds of refugees who were driven from Hillsfar or who fled the destruction of Myth Drannor and who now shelter in hidden camps under the northern eaves of the Cormanthor Forest. If you grew up in the camps, you have never been to a settlement other than the village of Elventree. As a guest of the elves, you have learned their ways and the ways of the forest. You are also traumatized, as residual wild magic, energies released by the fall of Thultanar upon Myth Drannor, and the constant fear of raids hunting for non-humans to fight in Hillsfar's Arena, have taken their toll on you, as they have on everyone in the camps.

name: Courtier
summary: Your knowledge of how bureaucracies function lets you gain access to the records and inner workings of any noble court or government you encounter. You know who the movers and shakers are, whom to go to for the favors you seek, and what the current intrigues of interest in the group are.

name: Criminal
summary: You have a history of breaking the law, and you still keep contacts in the criminal underworld who can pass messages for you. The Spy variant uses the same rules.

tables.title: Criminal Specialty
entries: Blackmailer
Burglar
Enforcer
Fence
Highway robber
Hired killer
Pickpocket
Smuggler

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I always have a backup plan for when things go wrong.
I stay calm no matter what; I never lose my temper.
In a new place, the first thing I do is spot the valuables and the hiding places.
I'd rather make a friend than an enemy.
I'm slow to trust; the friendliest-looking people often hide the most.
I don't care about the odds, so don't tell me them.
Tell me I can't do something and I'll set out to prove you wrong.
The smallest insult makes me blow up.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Honor. I don't steal from others in the trade. (Lawful)
Freedom. Chains are meant to be broken, and so are the people who make them. (Chaotic)
Charity. I steal from the rich to help people in need. (Good)
Greed. I'll do whatever it takes to get rich. (Evil)
People. I'm loyal to my friends, not to any ideal; everyone else can rot. (Neutral)
Redemption. There's some good in everyone. (Good)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: I'm paying back a debt to a generous benefactor.
My crimes keep my family fed.
Something important was stolen from me, and I'll steal it back.
I'm going to be the greatest thief who ever lived.
I did something terrible and hope to make up for it someday.
Someone I loved died because of my mistake; it will never happen again.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: When I see something valuable, all I can think about is stealing it.
Choosing between money and friends, I usually pick money.
If there's a plan, I'll forget it, or ignore it.
I have a tell that gives me away when I lie.
I run the moment things look bad.
An innocent person is in prison for my crime, and that's fine by me.

name: Dimir Operative
summary: You have more than one identity. The one you wear most of the time makes you appear to be a member of a guild other than House Dimir. You have documentation, established acquaintances, and disguises that allow you to assume that persona and fit into the secondary guild.

name: Dissenter
summary: Even in the carefully constructed and curated city-state of Naktamun, and in the presence of the five gods, some people rebel against the doctrines of the God-Pharaoh. They don’t challenge the existence of the gods, of course, for those gods are visible nearly every day in the streets of the city. Nor do they question the fact of life after death, which is plain to see in the anointed mummies that surround them, as well as the marauding mummies outside the Hekma. Rather, these dissenters simply refuse to follow the ordained course of life that leads to the glorious afterlife.

name: Dragon Casualty
summary: When the Maimed Virulence descended upon Phlan, you were one of the unfortunate casualties of war. Captured during the initial assault, you have spent the last year of your life as a plaything of a capricious and malevolent overlord.

choices.label: Special tool proficiency
choices.note: See this background origin for the exact tool proficiency.

name: Earthspur Miner
summary: You are a down-on-your-luck miner from the Earthspur Mountains who is no stranger to hardship. You have spent a great deal of time living among the dwarves, goliaths, and denizens of the Underdark who also work mines in the area. At this point, you're just as comfortable working underground as above. You know how to read a seam, dicker for supplies with the deep gnomes, party with dwarves, and find your way back to the surface afterward. Unfortunately, you haven't struck it rich… yet. Although you've come to Mulmaster looking for work, the tall peaks and deep mines of the Earthspurs still call to you.

name: Entertainer
summary: You thrive in front of an audience as a musician, dancer, actor, storyteller or other performer. You can always find a place to perform in exchange for food and lodging. The Gladiator variant uses the same rules.

tables.title: Entertainer Routine
entries: Actor
Dancer
Fire-eater
Jester
Juggler
Instrumentalist
Poet
Singer
Storyteller
Tumbler

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I have a story for every situation.
In every new town I pick up the local gossip and pass it on.
I'm a hopeless romantic, always looking for my one true love.
Nobody stays angry with me for long; I can defuse any tension.
I love a good insult, even one aimed at me.
I sulk when I'm not the center of attention.
Nothing less than perfect will do.
My moods change as fast as a song changes key.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Beauty. My performances make the world better than it was. (Good)
Tradition. The old songs and stories tell us who we are and must be kept. (Lawful)
Creativity. The world needs new ideas and bold action. (Chaotic)
Greed. I'm only in it for the money and the fame. (Evil)
People. I like seeing people smile when I perform; that's all. (Neutral)
Honesty. Art should show who you really are. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: My instrument is my most treasured possession and reminds me of someone I love.
Someone stole my beloved instrument, and one day I'll get it back.
I want to be famous, whatever it takes.
I try to live up to a hero of the old tales.
I'll do anything to prove I'm better than my hated rival.
I'd do anything for the members of my old troupe.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I'll do anything to win fame and renown.
A pretty face makes me lose my head.
A scandal keeps me from going home, and trouble seems to follow me.
I once mocked a noble who still wants my head, and I'd probably do it again.
I can't hide what I feel, and my sharp tongue gets me in trouble.
I try, but my friends can't count on me.

name: Faceless
summary: A faceless character adventures behind a mask of a public persona. This persona is as natural to them as their hidden, true face, but it disguises their identity. Roll on the Faceless Persona table to determine your persona, or work with the DM to create a persona that's unique to your character and suits the tone of your game.

name: Faction Agent
summary: The lack of large, centralized governments in the North and along the Sword Coast is likely directly responsible for the proliferation of secret societies and conspiracies in those lands. If your background is as an agent for one of the main factions of the North and Sword Coast, here are some possibilities.
skillProficiencies: Insight and one Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma skill of your choice, as appropriate to your faction

name: Failed Merchant
summary: Maybe you come from a long line of merchants. Perhaps you were an entrepreneur. Regardless. your ventures ended poorly. Whether it was because of outside influences, bad luck, or simply because your business acumen was weak, you lost everything.

name: Far Traveler
summary: A far traveler might have set out on a journey for one of a number of reasons, and the departure from his or her homeland could have been voluntary or involuntary. To determine why you are so far from home, roll on the table below or choose from the options provided. The following section, discussing possible homelands, includes some suggested reasons that are appropriate for each location.

choices.label: Choose one gaming set or musical instrument

name: Feylost
summary: You were transformed in some small way by your stay in the Feywild and gained a fey mark, determined by rolling on the Fey Mark table.

tables.title: Fey Mark
tables.note: Your stay in the Feywild changed you a little. The background says to roll; you can also pick.
entries: Your eyes shimmer through every color of the rainbow.
You smell faintly sweet, like honey or nectar.
You have long whiskers, like a cat's.
Your ears are pointed and tipped with soft fur.
Your skin glitters faintly under moonlight.
Flowers near you bloom or wilt, as you wish.
Your hair is a tangle of vines or brambles that grows back fast when cut.
You have a small animal tail, like a dog's.

tables.title: Feywild Visitor
tables.note: Sometimes, while you sleep or trance on a long rest, a spirit from the Feywild visits you. It means no harm and leaves only a memory. The DM decides when it happens; this table says what shape it takes.
entries: An awakened animal or plant
A centaur
A dryad
A faerie dragon
A pixie
A satyr
A sprite
A unicorn

tables.title: Personality Trait
entries: I keep hearing fey laughter. It is probably in my head.
I can't stay in one place for long; the road keeps calling.
A beautiful song can bring me to tears.
I carry a little piece of home with me, and share it.
Everything still fills me with a child's wonder.
Every new idea thrills me, until a newer one comes along.
I live by my own odd rules, and they make sense to me.
Grown-ups make me suspicious.

tables.title: Ideal
entries: Friendship. I never leave a friend behind. (Good)
Empathy. Nobody should have to suffer. (Good)
Wanderlust. The path nobody takes is the one for me. (Chaotic)
Changeability. Rules shift, so I shift with them. (Chaotic)
Honor. A deal is a deal, and I keep mine. (Lawful)
Rule of Three. Things come in threes, and I watch for them. (Lawful)
Obsession. I never let go of a grudge. (Evil)
Greed. I take what I want, whoever gets hurt. (Evil)

tables.title: Bond
entries: My word is everything; I never break it.
Magic pulls me in, especially where it runs thick.
I protect the wild places of the world.
One trusted friend means more to me than anything.
I will not harm a fey creature.
The Witchlight Carnival feels like home to me.
I long to go back to the Feywild.
I owe a debt to Mister Witch and Mister Light.

tables.title: Flaw
entries: I lose track of time and I'm always late.
I'm sure the whole multiverse is out to get me.
I cling to schedules and get anxious when plans slip.
Shiny, sparkly things tend to end up in my pockets.
I forget things, even simple ones.
I never give anything away without getting something back.
I have far too many vices.
I change my mind all the time.

name: Fisher
summary: You have spent your life aboard fishing vessels or combing the shallows for the bounty of the ocean. Perhaps you were born into a family of fisher folk, working with your kin to feed your village. Maybe the job was a means to an end - a way out of an undesirable circumstance that forced you to take up life aboard a ship. Regardless of how you began, you soon fell in love with the sea, the art of fishing, and the promise of the eternal horizon.

name: Folk Hero
summary: You previously pursued a simple profession among the peasantry, perhaps as a farmer, miner, servant, shepherd, woodcutter, or gravedigger. But something happened that set you on a different path and marked you for greater things. Choose or randomly determine a defining event that marked you as a hero of the people.

tables.title: Defining Event
entries: I stood up to a tyrant's soldiers.
I saved people during a natural disaster.
I stood alone against a terrible monster.
I stole from a corrupt merchant to help the poor.
I led a militia that fought off an invading army.
I broke into a tyrant's castle and stole weapons to arm the people.
I trained the peasantry to fight a tyrant's soldiers with farm tools.
A lord took back an unpopular decree after I led a symbolic protest.
A celestial, fey or similar creature blessed me or revealed my secret origin.
Recruited into a lord's army, I rose to leadership and was praised for my heroism.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I judge people by what they do, not what they say.
If someone is in trouble, I'm always ready to help.
Once I set my mind on something, I follow through no matter what.
I have a strong sense of fair play and always look for the fairest solution.
I'm confident in my abilities and try to build up others' confidence too.
Thinking is for other people; I prefer action.
I misuse long words to sound smart.
I get bored easily. When am I going to get on with my destiny?

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Respect. People deserve to be treated with dignity. (Good)
Fairness. No one should be above the law, rulers least of all. (Lawful)
Freedom. Tyrants must not be allowed to oppress the people. (Chaotic)
Might. If I become strong, I can take what I want, what I deserve. (Evil)
Sincerity. There's no good in pretending to be something I'm not. (Neutral)
Destiny. Nothing will turn me from my higher calling. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: My family is out there somewhere, and I hope to find them.
I worked the land, I love the land, and I'll protect it.
A proud noble once beat me badly; I take revenge on every bully I meet.
My tools are symbols of my past life, and I carry them to remember my roots.
I protect people who can't protect themselves.
I wish my childhood sweetheart had come with me to chase my destiny.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: The tyrant who rules my land will stop at nothing to see me dead.
I'm so sure of my destiny that I ignore my weaknesses and the risk of failure.
The people who knew me as a child know my shameful secret, so I can't go home.
I have a weakness for the vices of the city, especially hard drink.
Secretly, I think things would be better if I were the tyrant.
I have trouble trusting my allies.

name: Gambler
summary: All you need to make a lot of gold is a little gold. Except at those times when all you need to have no gold at all is a little gold. Whether you're a good gambler or a bad one rarely matters, because no one can divine the whims of Lady Luck. Sometimes you're up, sometimes you're down. But the thing about gambling is that someone is always willing to take a bet.

name: Gate Urchin
summary: All traffic into and out of the City of Trade passes through the Hillsfar Gate, making it the ideal place for the destitute to gather to panhandle, busk, gossip, and pick pockets. You grew up on the streets in the shadow of that great steel edifice, which houses both Red Plumes and Guild Mages. Though you may have moved on, you still have friends among them, and that life has had a lasting impact on you.

name: Gate Warden
summary: You grew up in one of the Outlands gate-towns, where the influence of a neighbouring Outer Plane shaped your daily life. Requires a Planescape campaign.

name: Giant Foundling
summary: How you came to live among colossal creatures is up to you to determine, but the Foundling Origin table suggests a variety of possibilities.
source: Bigby Presents - Glory of the Giants

name: Golgari Agent
summary: You know hidden, underground pathways that you can use to bypass crowds, obstacles, and observation as you move through the city. When you aren't in combat, you and companions you lead can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your speed would normally allow. The paths of the undercity are haunted by dangers that rarely brave the light of the surface world, so your journey isn't guaranteed to be safe.

name: Grinner
summary: All members of the Golden Grin have learned a handful of folk songs in their travels, and use those songs to send secret codes and alert fellow Grinners to danger. Choose a favorite song or roll on the Favorite Code-Songs table.

name: Gruul Anarch
summary: You are intimately familiar with areas of the city that most people shun: ruined neighborhoods where wurms rampaged, overgrown parks that no hand has tended in decades, and the vast, sprawling rubblebelts of broken terrain that civilized folk have long abandoned. You can find a suitable place for you and your allies to hide or rest in these areas. In addition, you can find food and fresh water in these areas for yourself and up to five other people each day.

name: Guild Artisan
summary: Instead of an artisans' guild, you might belong to a guild of traders, caravan masters, or shopkeepers. You don't craft items yourself but earn a living by buying and selling the works of others (or the raw materials artisans need to practice their craft). Your guild might be a large merchant consortium (or family) with interests across the region. Perhaps you transported goods from one place to another, by ship, wagon, or caravan, or bought them from traveling traders and sold them in your own little shop. In some ways, the traveling merchant's life lends itself to adventure far more than the life of an artisan.

tables.title: Guild Business
entries: Alchemists and apothecaries
Armorers, locksmiths and finesmiths
Brewers, distillers and vintners
Calligraphers, scribes and scriveners
Carpenters, roofers and plasterers
Cartographers, surveyors and chart-makers
Cobblers and shoemakers
Cooks and bakers
Glassblowers and glaziers
Jewelers and gemcutters
Leatherworkers, skinners and tanners
Masons and stonecutters
Painters, limners and sign-makers
Potters and tile-makers
Shipwrights and sailmakers
Smiths and metal-forgers
Tinkers, pewterers and casters
Wagon-makers and wheelwrights
Weavers and dyers
Woodcarvers, coopers and bowyers

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I believe anything worth doing is worth doing right; I can't help it.
I'm a snob who looks down on people who can't appreciate fine art.
I always want to know how things work and what makes people tick.
I'm full of sayings and proverbs for every situation.
I'm rude to people who lack my commitment to hard work and fair play.
I like to talk at length about my trade.
I don't part with my money easily and haggle for the best deal.
I'm well known for my work and expect people to recognize me.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Community. Civilized people must strengthen the bonds of community and civilization. (Lawful)
Generosity. My talents were given to me so I could help the world. (Good)
Freedom. Everyone should be free to make a living the way they choose. (Chaotic)
Greed. I'm only in it for the money. (Evil)
People. I'm loyal to the people I care about, not to ideals. (Neutral)
Aspiration. I work hard to be the best there is at my craft. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: The workshop where I learned my trade is the most important place in the world to me.
I made a masterwork for someone who didn't deserve it, and I'm still looking for someone who does.
I owe my guild a great debt for making me who I am.
I want to get rich to win someone's love.
One day I'll return to my guild and prove I'm the best artisan of them all.
I'll get revenge on the evil forces that destroyed my business and ruined my life.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I'll do nearly anything to get my hands on something rare or priceless.
I'm quick to assume someone is trying to cheat me.
No one must know I once stole money from the guild treasury.
I'm never satisfied with what I have; I always want more.
I would kill for a noble title.
I'm horribly jealous of anyone who outdoes my work. Rivals are everywhere.

name: Harborfolk
summary: You are one of the hundreds of small-time fishermen and -women who haul the bounty of Mulmaster's freshwater harbor to the city's markets each morning. You have spent countless days rowing in the waters in and around Mulmaster and know them and the other fisher folk, dockworkers, and port inhabitants better than anyone. Though you have left that life behind, you still visit once in a while.

name: Haunted One
summary: You are haunted by something so terrible that you dare not speak of it. You have seen horrors firsthand, and monster hunters and occultists recognise a kindred spirit in you.
skillProficiencies: Choose two of Arcana, Investigation, Religion, or Survival

name: Hermit
summary: You lived in seclusion for a formative part of your life, in a sheltered community or entirely alone, and during that time you discovered something unique and important.

tables.title: Life of Seclusion
entries: I was searching for spiritual enlightenment.
I was living in a religious community, following its rules.
I was exiled for a crime I didn't commit.
I withdrew from society after a life-changing event.
I needed a quiet place to work on my art, writing, music or manifesto.
I needed to commune with nature, far from civilization.
I was the caretaker of an ancient ruin or relic.
I was a pilgrim searching for a holy person, place or relic.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I've been alone so long that I barely speak; gestures and grunts will do.
I stay calm even in the face of disaster.
The leader of my old community taught me wise sayings, and I share them constantly.
I feel great sympathy for everyone who suffers.
Manners and social expectations mean nothing to me.
Everything that happens is part of a greater plan.
I often get lost in thought and forget what's around me.
I'm working on a grand philosophical theory and love to talk about it.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Greater Good. My gifts are meant to be shared with everyone, not used for myself. (Good)
Logic. Emotions must not cloud what is right and true. (Lawful)
Free Thinking. Curiosity and questions are what move the world forward. (Chaotic)
Power. Solitude and thought lead to mystical or magical power. (Evil)
Live and Let Live. Getting involved in other people's business only causes trouble. (Neutral)
Self-Knowledge. If you truly know yourself, there's nothing left to know. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: Nothing matters more to me than the others of my hermitage, order or group.
I went into seclusion to hide from people who may still be hunting me; one day I'll face them.
I'm still looking for the enlightenment I sought in my seclusion.
I went into seclusion because I loved someone I could never have.
If my discovery became known, it could bring ruin on the world.
In my isolation I found a great evil that only I can destroy.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: Now that I'm back in the world, I enjoy its pleasures a bit too much.
I hide dark, bloodthirsty thoughts that my isolation never cured.
I'm rigid in my beliefs and philosophy.
I have to win arguments, even at the cost of a friendship.
I'd take great risks to find a lost piece of knowledge.
I like keeping secrets and won't share them with anyone.

name: Hillsfar Merchant
summary: , { "refreshTime": 30, "renderVisibleOnly": false, "refreshVisibleOnly": true, "sizes": [ [ 160, 600 ] ], "report": { "enabled": true, "wording": "Report Ad", "position": "bottom-right" }, "mediaQuery": "(min-width: 1000px)" });

name: Hillsfar Smuggler
summary: Hillsfar is the City of Trade. However, the Great Law of Trade only protects "legitimate" trade, trade that passes through the city's sole gate, which the Red Plumes monitor and tax. And the Great Law of Humanity banishes non-humans from the city altogether. The two Great Laws create great demand and great risk for smugglers, who shepherd illicit goods and non-humans into and out of the city by secret routes. The Rogues' Guild tightly controls all of this activity, taking its cut from sanctioned jobs and exacting punishment for independent jobs.

name: House Agent
summary: You are an agent of one of Eberron's dragonmarked houses. Your house gives you contacts, resources and a mission, and expects your loyalty in return.
source: Eberron - Rising from the Last War

choices.label: Choose two House tool proficiencies
choices.note: Use the House Tool Proficiencies table for this background.

name: Inheritor
summary: You are the heir to something of great value: an item, a title, a secret or a piece of land. Others may want what you inherited, and you must decide what to do with it.
skillProficiencies: Survival, plus one from among Arcana, History, and Religion

choices.label: Choose one gaming set or musical instrument

name: Initiate
summary: Your life is oriented around your participation in the five trials that will determine your worthiness in the afterlife. While you prepare for and undergo those trials, you have constant access to training. A comfortable place to live and regular meals are provided to you by servitor mummies (the anointed) under the supervision of viziers. You can enjoy these benefits only as long as you obey the societal norms of Naktamun—training for the trials (with or without your crop), obeying the orders of the gods, and following the instructions of their viziers. If you violate these norms, you risk being treated as a dissenter.

name: Inquisitor
summary: As an inquisitor of the church, you have the authority to arrest criminals. In the absence of other authorities, you are authorized to pass judgment and even carry out sentencing. If you abuse this power, however, your superiors in the church might strip it from you.

name: Investigator (VRGR)
summary: You hunt for the truth behind crimes and mysteries, whether as a constable, a private detective or a curious amateur. Your first case shaped the kinds of mysteries you chase.
skillProficiencies: Choose two from among Insight, Investigation, or Perception

name: Iron Route Bandit
summary: The Iron Route, once the primary trade route between Phlan and Zhentil Keep, used to be a site of extensive banditry until the Phlan’s recent occupation. Your time as an erstwhile bandit has given you plenty of experience in the saddle and a knack for acquiring and appraising other people’s mounts, pets, and vehicles among other things. This particular set of skills has become very lucrative for you by working for the underground as a horse thief for a local guild of thieves and other shadowy organizations.

name: Izzet Engineer
summary: The popular conception of the Izzet League is based on mad inventions, dangerous experiments, and explosive blasts. Much of that perception is accurate, but the league is also involved with mundane tasks of construction and architecture- primarily in crafting the infrastructure that allows Ravnicans to enjoy running water, levitating platforms, and other magical and technological wonders.

name: Knight of Solamnia
summary: You trained as a squire of the Knights of Solamnia, sworn to the Oath and the Measure. This background grants the Squire of Solamnia feat.
source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen

name: Knight of the Order
summary: Many who rightfully call themselves "knight" earn that title as part of an order in service to a deity, such as Kelemvor's Eternal Order or Mystra's Knights of the Mystic Fire. Other knightly orders serve a government, royal family, or are the elite military of a feudal state, such as the brutal Warlock Knights of Vaasa. Other knighthoods are secular and non-governmental organizations of warriors who follow a particular philosophy, or consider themselves a kind of extended family, similar to an order of monks. Although there are organizations, such as the Knights of the Shield, that use the trappings of knighthood without necessarily being warriors, most folk of Faerûn who hear the word "knight" think of a mounted warrior in armor beholden to a code. Below are a few knightly organizations.
skillProficiencies: Persuasion, plus one from among Arcana, History, Nature, and Religion, as appropriate for your order

choices.label: Choose one gaming set or musical instrument

name: Lorehold Student
summary: You gain the Strixhaven Initiate feat and must choose Lorehold within it.

name: Mage of High Sorcery
summary: You gain the Initiate of High Sorcery feat.
source: Dragonlance: Shadow of the Dragon Queen

name: Marine
summary: You were trained for battle on sandy beaches and rocky shores. You have launched midnight raids from swift ships whose names evoke terror in the hearts of your adversaries. The water is your second home, the rain your shelter, and the crashing waves your battle cry.

name: Mercenary Veteran
summary: Countless mercenary companies operate up and down the Sword Coast and throughout the North. Most are small-scale operations that employ a dozen to a hundred folk who offer security services, hunt monsters and brigands, or go to war in exchange for gold. Some organizations, such as the Zhentarim, Flaming Fist, and the nation of Mintarn have hundreds or thousands of members and can provide private armies to those with enough funds. A few organizations operating in the North are described below.

name: Mulmaster Aristocrat
summary: From your hilltop home, you have looked down (literally and perhaps figuratively) on the unwashed masses of Mulmaster for your entire life. Your fur-trimmed robes and training in the visual and performing arts mark you as wealthy and perhaps well-born; you are a member of the City of Danger's aristocracy.

name: Noble
summary: You were born into wealth, power and privilege, and people of high society treat you as one of their own. Knights can take the Retainers feature in place of Position of Privilege.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I flatter everyone I meet and make them feel special.
The common folk love me for my kindness and generosity.
One look at my bearing tells you I'm a cut above the rest.
I take great care to look my best and follow the latest fashion.
Hard work and poor lodgings are beneath me.
I may be noble by birth, but I don't think I'm better than anyone else.
Once you lose my favor, you never get it back.
Insult me and I'll ruin you, your name and your family.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Respect. People owe me respect because of my station, but everyone deserves dignity. (Good)
Responsibility. I respect those above me, and those below me must respect me. (Lawful)
Independence. I must prove I can manage without my family's help. (Chaotic)
Power. If I gain enough power, no one will tell me what to do. (Evil)
Family. Blood runs thicker than water. (Any)
Noble Obligation. I must protect and care for the people beneath me. (Good)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: I'll face any challenge to win my family's approval.
My house's alliance with another noble family must be kept at all costs.
Nothing is more important than the rest of my family.
I'm in love with the heir of a family my own family hates.
My loyalty to my sovereign never wavers.
The common people must see me as their hero.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: Secretly, I think everyone else is beneath me.
I hide a scandal that could ruin my family forever.
I hear veiled insults and threats in everything and anger quickly.
I have an endless appetite for pleasure.
In fact, the world does revolve around me.
What I say and do often brings shame on my family.

name: Orzhov Representative
summary: You serve the Orzhov Syndicate of Ravnica, a guild of wealthy oligarchs and indebted spirits. You can call on lower-ranking guild members for help.

name: Outlander
summary: You've been to strange places and seen things that others cannot begin to fathom. Consider some of the distant lands you have visited, and how they impacted you. You can roll on the following table to determine your occupation during your time in the wild, or choose one that best fits your character.

tables.title: Origin
entries: Forester
Trapper
Homesteader
Guide
Exile or outcast
Bounty hunter
Pilgrim
Tribal nomad
Hunter-gatherer
Tribal marauder

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I'm driven by a wanderlust that took me away from home.
I watch over my friends as if they were newborn pups.
I once ran for miles without stopping to warn my clan of danger, and I'd do it again.
I have a lesson for every situation, taken from watching nature.
I have no use for the rich and well-mannered; money and manners won't save you from a hungry bear.
I'm always fiddling absently with things I pick up.
I'm far more comfortable around animals than people.
I was, in fact, raised by wolves.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Change. Life is like the seasons; it is always changing, and so must we. (Chaotic)
Greater Good. Everyone has to do their part for the good of the tribe. (Good)
Honor. If I dishonor myself, I dishonor my whole clan. (Lawful)
Might. The strongest are meant to rule. (Evil)
Nature. The natural world matters more than all the works of civilization. (Neutral)
Glory. I must earn glory in battle, for myself and my clan. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: My family, clan or tribe is the most important thing in my life, even far from them.
Harm done to the wild places of my home is harm done to me.
I'll bring terrible vengeance on the evildoers who destroyed my homeland.
I am the last of my tribe, and it's up to me to keep their names alive.
I have terrible visions of a coming disaster and will do anything to stop it.
It is my duty to have children to carry on my tribe.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I'm far too fond of ale, wine and other drink.
There's no room for caution in a life lived to the fullest.
I remember every insult and hold a quiet grudge.
I'm slow to trust people of other peoples and tribes.
Violence is my answer to almost every problem.
Don't expect me to save people who can't save themselves; that's how nature works.

name: Phlan Insurgent
summary: The taking of Phlan by Vorgansharax is a clear memory in your mind. You were going about your everyday business when the green dragon's forces spilled out of the sewers and assailed your home. Many of Phlan's citizens, young and old alike, were captured, killed, or offered as tribute to the Maimed Virulence. You, yourself, were one of those captured. But, either with the help of adventurers or through your own wits and sheer determination, you escaped.

name: Phlan Refugee
summary: Gone are the happier days of walking into the Laughing Goblin Inn after a hard day’s labor. Everything has changed, and you are lucky to be alive. Back in Phlan you could count yourself among those street-wise folks who knew when to pay a bribe and who to work with to make a living. Your ability to listen to the winds of change have saved you before, and this time they allowed you to be one of the lucky few who escaped Phlan with something more than just the shirt on your back.

name: Plaintiff
summary: Sure, accidents happen. But they seem to happen an awful lot when Acquisitions Incorporated operatives are on the scene. Naturally, nothing ever happens when there are no witnesses left behind. But sometimes one casualty is left a little less than dead, just waiting to discover what a lucky break that accident actually was.

name: Planar Philosopher
summary: You belong to one of Sigil's factions and hold firm beliefs about the nature of the multiverse. Requires a Planescape campaign.
skillProficiencies: Arcana, the skill associated with your faction (see the Sigil Faction Affinities table) or one skill of your choice.

name: Prismari Student
summary: You gain the Strixhaven Initiate feat and must choose Prismari within it.

choices.label: Choose one artisan's tool or musical instrument

name: Quandrix Student
summary: You gain the Strixhaven Initiate feat and must choose Quandrix within it.

name: Rakdos Cultist
summary: Rakdos performance styles typically fuse standard circus-style acrobatics with fire, wrought-iron spikes and hooks, and monsters. You can roll a d8 or choose from the options in the Performance Options table to determine your preferred style of performance.

name: Rewarded
summary: You were living a difficult life before your destiny suddenly changed through a miraculous turn of good fortune. Perhaps a benevolent deity gave you precisely what you most desired. You might have stumbled across a Deck of Many Things and drawn a card with a potent, positive effect. Or maybe you inherited a modest fortune from a distant relative you didn’t know you had.

name: Rival Intern
summary: You were an intern at a rival of Acquisitions Incorporated, and you gained a healthy respect for not just the job and the franchising opportunities. but for the ruthless and efficient way Acquisitions Incorporated goes about its business. Why deal with the rest, when you can work for the best?

name: Ruined
summary: Everything was going so well! You had a life of luxury, love, and comfort when you suddenly lost it all. Perhaps you were framed for crimes you didn’t commit and lost your reputation, fortune, and career. Maybe a rampaging dragon or another monster wiped out everything you had in a single calamitous afternoon. Or you might have sought out a Deck of Many Things, hoping to make your successful life even more glorious—only to draw a destructive card that changed your destiny forever.

name: Rune Carver
summary: Each rune carver has a unique style and preferred medium. To determine how you make your runes, you can roll on the Rune Style table..
source: Bigby Presents - Glory of the Giants

name: Sage
summary: You spent years learning the lore of the multiverse through manuscripts, scrolls and the teaching of experts. When you don't know a piece of information, you often know where to find it.
equipment: Letter from a dead colleague posing a question you have not yet answered

tables.title: Specialty
entries: Alchemist
Astronomer
Discredited academic
Librarian
Professor
Researcher
Wizard's apprentice
Scribe

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I use long, fancy words to sound learned.
I've read every book in the world's greatest libraries, or I like to say I have.
I'm used to explaining things to people less clever than me, and I'm patient about it.
Nothing excites me more than a good mystery.
I listen to every side of an argument before making up my mind.
I talk slowly and carefully to people, as if they were a bit dim.
I'm terribly awkward in social situations.
I'm sure people are always trying to steal my secrets.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Knowledge. Knowledge is the path to power and self-improvement. (Neutral)
Beauty. Beautiful things point us toward what is true. (Good)
Logic. Emotions must not cloud our thinking. (Lawful)
No Limits. Nothing should hold back the endless possibilities of existence. (Chaotic)
Power. Knowledge is the way to power and control. (Evil)
Self-Improvement. The point of study is to make yourself better. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: It is my duty to protect my students.
I have an ancient text full of terrible secrets that must not fall into the wrong hands.
I work to preserve a library, university, scriptorium or monastery.
My life's work is a series of books on one subject.
I've been searching all my life for the answer to one question.
I sold my soul for knowledge, and I hope to win it back with great deeds.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: The promise of new knowledge pulls me away from anything else.
Most people run from a demon; I'd stop to study its anatomy.
Unlocking an ancient mystery is worth the price of a civilization.
I miss obvious answers while chasing complicated ones.
I speak without thinking and often insult people.
I can't keep a secret to save my life, or anyone else's.

name: Sailor
summary: You spent your youth under the sway of a dread pirate, a ruthless cutthroat who taught you how to survive in a world of sharks and savages. You've indulged in larceny on the high seas and sent more than one deserving soul to a briny grave. Fear and bloodshed are no strangers to you, and you've garnered a somewhat unsavory reputation in many a port town.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: My friends know they can rely on me, no matter what.
I work hard so that I can play hard once the work is done.
I love sailing into new ports and making friends over a drink.
I stretch the truth for the sake of a good story.
To me, a tavern brawl is a nice way to get to know a new city.
I never pass up a friendly wager.
My language is as foul as it gets.
I like a job well done, especially if someone else does it.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Respect. A ship holds together on respect between captain and crew. (Good)
Fairness. We all do the work, so we all share the rewards. (Lawful)
Freedom. The sea is freedom: the freedom to go anywhere and do anything. (Chaotic)
Mastery. I'm a predator, and the other ships on the sea are my prey. (Evil)
People. I'm committed to my crewmates, not to ideals. (Neutral)
Aspiration. Someday I'll have my own ship and chart my own course. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: My loyalty to my captain comes first; everything else is second.
The ship matters most; crews and captains come and go.
I'll always remember my first ship.
In a harbor town I have a sweetheart whose eyes nearly kept me from the sea.
I was cheated out of my fair share of the profits, and I want what's mine.
Pirates killed my captain and crew, took our ship and left me to die. Vengeance will be mine.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: I follow orders even when I think they're wrong.
I'll say anything to get out of extra work.
If someone questions my courage, I never back down, however dangerous it is.
Once I start drinking, it's hard for me to stop.
I can't help pocketing loose coins and other trinkets.
My pride will probably be the end of me.

name: Secret Identity
summary: Even though you are a non-human, despite Hillsfar's Great Law of Humanity, you continue to live in the City of Trade. You do so by maintaining a secret identity, forging documents, and even wearing a disguise. Few, if any, know you aren't human.

name: Selesnya Initiate
summary: As a member of the Selesnya Conclave, you can count on your guild mates to provide shelter and aid. You and your companions can find a place to hide or rest in any Selesnya enclave in the city, unless you have proven to be a danger to them. The members of the enclave will shield you from the law or anyone else searching for you, though they will not risk their lives in this effort.

choices.label: Choose one artisan's tool or musical instrument

name: Shade Fanatic
summary: You grew up at a time when the wizards of Netheril were at war with the elves of Cormanthor. You recall sitting crosslegged hearing the stories of the glorious Thultanthar, also called the Shade Enclave and the City of Shade, and aspired to study there and maybe even did, for a time. Your dreams came crashing down a few years ago when Thultanthar fell from the sky upon Myth Drannor.

name: Shipwright
summary: You have sailed into war on the decks of great ships, patching their hulls with soup bowls and prayers. You once helped build a fishing vessel that single-handedly saved a town from starvation. You have seen a majestic prow in your dreams that you have not been able to replicate in wood. Since childhood, you have loved the water and have been captivated by the many vessels that travel on it.

name: Silverquill Student
summary: You gain the Strixhaven Initiate feat and must choose Silverquill within it.

name: Simic Scientist
summary: As a Simic researcher, you are part of a clade - a diverse group of individuals combining disparate talents in pursuit of a common goal - or a researcher on a specialized, short-term project focused on addressing an immediate need. You can roll a d6 or choose from the options in the Research Options table to determine your area of research.

name: Smuggler
summary: On a rickety barge, you carried a hundred longswords in fish barrels right past the dock master's oblivious lackeys. You have paddled a riverboat filled with stolen elven wine under the gaze of the moon and sold it for twice its value in the morning. In your more charitable times, you have transported innocents out of war zones or helped guide herd animals to safety on the banks of a burning river.

name: Soldier
summary: You served in an army or militia and learned discipline, rank and the realities of war. Your military rank still carries weight with soldiers of your former organization.

tables.title: Specialty
entries: Officer
Scout
Infantry
Cavalry
Healer
Quartermaster
Standard bearer
Support staff (cook, blacksmith or the like)

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I'm always polite and respectful.
I'm haunted by memories of war and can't get the violence out of my head.
I've lost too many friends, and I'm slow to make new ones.
I'm full of inspiring and cautionary stories from my service for almost any fight.
I can stare down a hell hound without flinching.
I enjoy being strong and like breaking things.
I have a crude sense of humor.
I face problems head-on; a simple, direct solution is the best way to success.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Greater Good. It is our duty to give our lives to protect others. (Good)
Responsibility. I do what I must and obey just authority. (Lawful)
Independence. Blindly following orders is a kind of tyranny. (Chaotic)
Might. In life as in war, the stronger side wins. (Evil)
Live and Let Live. Ideals aren't worth killing over or going to war for. (Neutral)
Nation. My city, nation or people are all that matter. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: I would still give my life for the people I served with.
Someone saved my life on the battlefield. To this day, I never leave a friend behind.
My honor is my life.
I'll never forget the crushing defeat my company suffered or the enemies who caused it.
Those who fight beside me are worth dying for.
I fight for those who cannot fight for themselves.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: The monstrous enemy we faced in battle still makes me tremble with fear.
I have little respect for anyone who isn't a proven warrior.
I made a terrible mistake in battle that cost many lives, and I'd do anything to keep it secret.
My hatred of my enemies is blind and unreasoning.
I obey the law, even when the law causes misery.
I'd rather eat my armor than admit I'm wrong.

name: Stojanow Prisoner
summary: Those words still haunt your dreams at night. When everyone was fleeing Phlan, you chose to stay. Whether out of an emotional attachment, or pursuit of riches, you made the decision that would affect the rest of your life.

name: Ticklebelly Nomad
summary: You were born into a nomadic tribe that called the Ticklebelly Hills home. You migrated from location to location, living off the land with your tribe. The tribe would seasonally travel south into the Grass Sea and the Giant’s Cairn, north into the Dragonspine Mountains, and even occasionally east across the Stojanow River to the borders of the Quivering Forest. In your migrations, your people have come to know the stone giant tribes that populate the Giant’s Cairn.

name: Trade Sheriff
summary: You are one of the many people that make sure the trade routes are clear at ALL times. You assure that theGreat Law of Tradeis followed at all costs. You work by yourself or in groups to quell bandits and brigands who might stop trade routes from going through. You investigate potential ambushes and possible rumors as to someone wanting to rob or stop caravans. You are as much an investigator as you are law enforcement.

name: Urban Bounty Hunter
summary: You are in frequent contact with people in the segment of society that your chosen quarries move through. These people might be associated with the criminal underworld, the rough-and-tumble folk of the streets, or members of high society. This connection comes in the form of a contact in any city you visit, a person who provides information about the people and places of the local area.
skillProficiencies: Choose two from among Deception, Insight, Persuasion, and Stealth

name: Urchin
summary: You know the secret patterns and flow to cities and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you (and companions you lead) can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your speed would normally allow.

tables.title: Personality Trait
tables.note: Pick or roll one or two.
entries: I hide scraps of food and trinkets in my pockets.
I ask a lot of questions.
I like to squeeze into small places where no one can get to me.
I sleep with my back to a wall or tree, holding onto everything I own.
I eat like a pig and have terrible manners.
I think anyone who's nice to me is hiding something nasty.
I don't like to bathe.
I say out loud what other people only hint at or hide.

tables.title: Ideal
tables.note: What drives you.
entries: Respect. Everyone, rich or poor, deserves respect. (Good)
Community. We have to look after each other, because no one else will. (Lawful)
Change. The low are lifted up and the high brought down. Change is the way of things. (Chaotic)
Retribution. The rich need to be shown what life in the gutter is like. (Evil)
People. I help the people who help me; that's how we survive. (Neutral)
Aspiration. I'm going to prove that I deserve a better life than this. (Any)

tables.title: Bond
tables.note: Who or what you care about most.
entries: My town or city is my home, and I'll fight to defend it.
I support an orphanage to keep other children from going through what I did.
I owe my survival to another urchin who taught me to live on the streets.
I owe a debt I can never repay to the person who took pity on me.
I escaped poverty by robbing someone important, and now I'm wanted for it.
No one else should have to suffer what I went through.

tables.title: Flaw
tables.note: A weakness others could use against you.
entries: If I'm outnumbered, I run away.
Gold looks like a lot of money to me, and I'll do just about anything for more of it.
I'll never fully trust anyone other than myself.
I'd rather kill someone in their sleep than fight fair.
It's not stealing if I need it more than someone else.
People who can't take care of themselves get what they deserve.

name: Uthgardt Tribe Member
summary: Though this section details the Uthgardt specifically, either it or theOutlanderbackground can be used for a character whose origin lies with one of the other barbarian tribes in Faerûn.

choices.label: Choose one artisan's tool or musical instrument

name: Vizier
summary: Your voice is the voice of your god, at least in theory. Your job might include training and instructing initiates, and they are required to obey you. In any circumstance, an initiate is expected to defer to your voice and obey your commands. If you abuse this authority, though, your god might personally punish you.

name: Volstrucker Agent
summary: Happy people aren't selected to join the Volstrucker. The Cerberus Assembly preys upon talented individuals who have been broken by tragedy - in some cases, tragedy that the Volstrucker has arranged for. A slightly broken mind is more easily reshaped and reeducated. Choose the tragedy that set you on this path, or roll on the Tragedies table.

name: Waterdhavian Noble
summary: While you are in Waterdeep or elsewhere in the North your house sees to your everyday needs. Your name and signet are sufficient to cover most of your expenses; the inns, taverns, and festhalls you frequent are glad to record your debt and send an accounting to your family's estate in Waterdeep to settle what you owe.

choices.label: Choose one gaming set or musical instrument

name: Wildspacer
summary: You had a harrowing encounter with one of Wildspace’s many terrors. You escaped with your life, but the encounter left you with a scar or two, or perhaps a recurring nightmare. Roll on the Close Encounter table to determine which creature nearly got the best of you.
source: Spelljamer: Adventures in Space - Astral Adventurer's Guide

name: Witchlight Hand
summary: Over the years, you have earned the friendship of another carnival fixture. Roll a d8 and consult the Carnival Companion table to determine whom or what you've befriended, or you can choose an option that you like. Work with your DM to flesh out this friendship. This companion hangs around you while you're in the carnival, but it won't voluntarily leave the carnival.

choices.label: Choose disguise kit or one musical instrument

name: Witherbloom Student
summary: You gain the Strixhaven Initiate feat and must choose Witherbloom within it.
